claims.statement: Poland's mandatory KSeF rollout covers remaining taxpayers from 1 April 2026 subject to a temporary small-sales exception through 2026.
The Ministry of Finance publishes an OpenAPI contract, SDKs, and production/integration environments for KSeF 2.0.
The VAT taxpayer registry supports automated checks of NIP or REGON against a bank account and returns an electronic confirmation key.

contrary_evidence: Government tools already provide free NIP-account verification and mass-check data, so a basic lookup has little defensibility.
KSeF bank-account fields are optional, limiting deterministic invoice-to-account matching.

economics.acquisition_route: Accounting-software integrations first, then finance-team referrals and bookkeeping channels
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 1200 customers averaging 500 PLN monthly plus usage revenue could reach about 7m PLN annual revenue; at 25% operating margin and 80% founder ownership, a profit-based business value plus accumulated cash could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 5-6
economics.founder_time: 3 hours/day for an API pilot, with security review and sales support contracted as needed
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 75-85% after registry calls, hosting, security, and manual escalation review
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 60 customers contributing roughly 800 PLN monthly gross margin could repay the pilot in 12-18 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 500-3000 PLN monthly minimum plus 0.10-0.50 PLN per checked invoice
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every payment run repeats; ERP integration and accumulated supplier history may support annual retention

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned cross-customer patterns, verified supplier histories, false-positive feedback, and workflow switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Polish mid-market finance teams, accounting platforms, and outsourced bookkeeping firms
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Integrations and revenue share with Polish accounting, ERP, and bookkeeping vendors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: API and review console combining KSeF fields, VAT whitelist checks, change detection, and auditable approvals
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Business or accounting platform pays monthly and/or per invoice verified before payment release
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A structured invoice arrives or supplier payment details change before an accounts-payable run

founder_fit: Direct match for data science, anomaly detection, and API automation
Polish regulatory and language context is useful
Channel sales can reduce constant founder-led outreach
risks: Handling financial and invoice data creates high security and liability exposure
False positives could delay legitimate payments
ERP incumbents or banks can bundle basic verification

structure.commercial_archetype: Per-transaction verification bureau and approval API
structure.control_point: The mandatory pre-payment approval call plus a permissioned history of verified supplier identities and account changes
structure.critical_dependency: Customers must grant lawful KSeF, ERP, and payment-workflow access and treat the signal as an approval gate

thesis: Embed a verification step between receipt of a structured KSeF invoice and ERP payment approval. The service checks invoice identity, NIP-account consistency, duplicate and change patterns, and customer-specific supplier history, while requiring human confirmation for anomalies. The defensible asset would be the permissioned supplier-change graph and position in the approval workflow, not access to public registries.
title: KSeF Supplier Payment Trust Gate
uncertainties: Whether customers will share enough permissioned outcomes to create a network advantage
Whether KSeF access scopes permit the intended integration model
The incremental willingness to pay beyond free government checks
